intro.title: Custom websites, with the calm of work done properly.
bio: I’m Nicolò Peruzzi, a web designer and developer. I work with restaurants, hotels, professional studios, gyms, and brands that have something real to say, but don’t know how to say it online.

Most of the sites I see are generic, built on templates, made to please everyone and useful to no one. I do the opposite: I always start with a real conversation with you. I learn how you work, what sets you apart, and what you want to happen when someone finds you online.

Then I build a site that actually communicates. It isn’t beautiful for the sake of being beautiful: it’s designed to bring bookings, concrete enquiries, and trust. A beautiful site that doesn’t work is just an expense.
intro.together: You don’t start with a form or a presentation. We talk. You tell me about your work, your clients, and what you aren’t managing to communicate. From there I design a strategy that makes sense for you, and I build it with care.

synth.description: A spatial wavetable synth in the browser: 3D sound, binaural listening, and cymatics.
synth.case: Into the Void is a personal spatial synthesizer in the browser.
synth.what: Into the Void is a spatial wavetable synth that runs in the browser: it generates sound, places it in 3D space, plays it back binaurally (HRTF), and draws a cymatics view of the signal. The live demo is at spatial-synth-symvolia.vercel.app/synth.
synth.why: To explore synthesis, space, and interaction in one instrument — beyond brochure sites — and to ship a public demo of the same engine that also exists as a plug-in (CLAP/AU/VST, macOS builds in Downloads).
synth.role: Personal project: interface (UI/UX), sound design (presets and engine behaviour), and engineering (audio engine + web UI). [TO COMPLETE: any collaboration or parts owned by others]
synth.stack: React 18 UI (UMD). Audio via the Web Audio API with an AudioWorklet (`ssc-synth`); ScriptProcessor fallback if the worklet is unavailable. Spatialisation with an HRTF model (Brown & Duda) and Ambisonics output (1st/3rd order) plus stereo. Field and cymatics on Canvas/WebGL (no Three.js in the analysed bundle). DSP core also in portable C++20 with a WASM path. A separate Next.js host covers the patch library site (Auth.js, Neon, Vercel Blob).
techChoices: AudioWorklet keeps DSP off the main thread, with a stable message protocol to the UI (params, notes, telemetry).
HRTF model and MagLS decoder aligned with the C++ core so web and plug-in share the same spatial idea.
3D field and cymatics on canvas: the Orbit layout keeps controls and the field on one screen; on mobile, tabs and clusters collapse.
No autoplay: `ensureAudio` / Start audio resume the AudioContext only after a user gesture (tap, click, or M).
challenges: Browser autoplay policy: audio stays off until interaction; Start audio / M unlock the context.
Performance: the worklet avoids saturating the main thread; visuals use requestAnimationFrame. [TO COMPLETE: concrete CPU/latency figures on reference devices]
Compatibility: from file:// or without a worklet the engine can fall back to ScriptProcessor on the main thread (documented in the core README).
Accessible mute/stop: Stop audio and the M shortcut; Escape / All notes off clears held notes.

velvet.description: Elegance and simplicity in service of the dining experience
velvet.case: A concept for fine dining: generous type, photography, and section rhythm guide people who are reading the menu and people who want to book, without visual noise. Reservations sit inside the visit, and the layout stays clear on a phone, where many last-minute decisions happen. Let guests feel the room before they walk in.

hotel.description: Digital hospitality that captures the character of the property
hotel.case: A hospitality concept: photography of the property is raw material. Rooms and the gallery are organised so visitors can choose, a stay request is reachable from anywhere on the page, and the layout keeps the same calm from phone to desktop. Tell a concrete story of hospitality — light, materials, place — and a clear step toward booking.

studio.description: Authority and trust in every pixel
studio.case: A concept for a professional studio: authority without coldness. The hierarchy puts expertise, method, and contact in the same glance. Forms are short, information is grouped by decision, and the tone stays precise. Someone arriving with a problem can see how to start a conversation, rather than meeting a wall of text.

gym.description: Energy and motivation, from the screen to the heart
gym.case: A fitness concept: bring the energy of the weight room onto the page without turning it into noise. Membership, a trial, and community read in a few seconds, with sharp contrast and a grid that holds on small screens. Motivate, then point to the next step: walk in, try it, join.

symvolia.description: Immersive artist site: cinematic threshold, Latin orbit nav, sound archive.
symvolia.case: Symvolia.xyz is a personal artist site for a sound designer / producer / DJ, built as an immersive experience rather than a brochure.
symvolia.what: Symvolia.xyz is the artist site for Symvolia (sound designer, producer, DJ): a static platform designed as an immersive experience — cinematic threshold, esoteric identity, sound archive — not a generic brochure. Live: https://symvolia.xyz/
symvolia.why: To give the artistic project a space that matches the language of sound and symbol: entering the site should feel like crossing a door, not opening a menu. It is also a personal lab for motion, WebGL, and branding without a commercial brief.
symvolia.role: Personal project: concept, UX, visual design, front-end (HTML/CSS/JS), threshold audio, and GitHub Pages publishing. [TO COMPLETE: any collaboration on copy, 3D assets, or mastering]
symvolia.stack: Static HTML/CSS/JS (no build step). Opening portal: Three.js (WebGL, post-processing, GLTF), GSAP timeline, Web Audio (`portal-audio.js`). Ambient and SFX via `<audio>` elements. Deployed on GitHub Pages with custom domain symvolia.xyz.
techChoices: UX — narrative threshold: the cinematic intro (eye → seal, ~8–10s, no hard black cuts) is the door; only after that do you reach the stage and archive. Returning with `?from=archive` skips the intro and lands in the library.

UX — Latin as identity: on the home orbit, links are Latin phrases (e.g. QUOD SUPERIUS / SICUT INFERIUS → Vision). Inside the archive, primary nav is English (Bio, Vision, Archive, Contact) and «Enter the Archive» has an English `aria-label` — so non-Latin readers can orient after the threshold. Today the Latin orbit items still lack per-link `aria-label`, tooltip, or secondary gloss: that is an open improvement.

Motion and performance: Three.js + vortex shader + particles, driven by GSAP; documented targets ~60 fps desktop (pixel ratio cap 2, ~90 particles) and 30+ on mobile/coarse pointer (pixel ratio 1.25, ~48 particles). Cost is concentrated on the threshold, not the whole session.

Assets: `rel=preload` on critical threshold images (emblem, seal, corona desktop/mobile via media queries); ambient and enter sounds with `preload="auto"`. Reveals and environments use IntersectionObserver where needed.

prefers-reduced-motion: with `reduce`, the portal is skipped and `symvolia:intro-complete` fires immediately; the same flag simplifies or disables motion across environment, archive, serpents, and related modules.
SEO for a highly visual site: title, meta description, and canonical are in place. Open Graph / Twitter Card and JSON-LD are missing — a known weakness for an image-led experience.
challenges: Keeping the threshold continuous (eye → gold → seal) without black flashes, with audio handoff into stage ambient.
Balancing immersion and accessibility: reduced-motion is covered; Latin orbit orientation is not yet (see above).
Loading heavy audio/visual assets on Pages without a bundler: targeted preloads + skipping the portal under reduced-motion.
wouldRedo: Add an `aria-label` (and/or gloss / tooltip) on every Latin orbit item in the page’s primary language, so identity stays but screen readers and non-Latin readers know the destination before entering.
Finish social SEO: Open Graph, Twitter Card, and maybe Person/MusicGroup JSON-LD — today sharing leans almost only on title + description.

process.title: Three phases, no useless rush.
process.lead: From the first conversation to launch, the path stays readable. You always know where we are.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.text: Listening and analysis: audience, offer, obstacles, and what counts as a result.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: Prototyping and iteration: structure, visual tone, and paths, revised until the page decides on its own.

steps.title: Launch
steps.text: Implementation and optimisation: build, performance, accessibility, and going live.

skills.title: Tools I use, not a display list.
skills.lead: I choose the stack for the project. The constant is an interface that is fast, clear, and easy to update.

notes.title: Project notes, not trends.
notes.lead: Three ideas that keep returning when I design a site for a real business.

items.title: The menu is not the website
items.text: A restaurant does not need a digital brochure. It needs a path: atmosphere, two dishes, a booking without friction. When the menu is the only job, the page stops working the moment someone is already convinced. I design the decision first, then the sections.

items.title: What I measure before launch
items.text: Response time, the weight of the first screen, the clarity of the main button. A slow or ambiguous page costs enquiries even when it is beautiful. Before publishing I check phone reading, contrast, keyboard focus, and the path to contact.

items.title: Trust, not ornament
items.text: Hotels, studios, and gyms sell different things, but visitors ask the same question: can I trust this? The answer sits in hierarchy, tone, and visual proof of the place. Ornament comes later, and only if it serves the message.

items.title: WCAG 2.1 AA
items.text: Contrast, visible focus, form labels, and a reading order that makes sense.

items.title: Core Web Vitals
items.text: Optimised images, little unnecessary JavaScript, a first screen that arrives quickly.

items.title: Technical SEO
items.text: Metadata, sitemap, alternate languages, and structured data search engines can read.

items.title: Custom design
items.text: Hierarchy shaped for the sector. No generic theme adapted at the last minute.

services.title: Four ways a website can work for you.
services.lead: I don't sell isolated pages. I build a path that makes the business recognisable and leads to the right enquiry.

items.title: Custom websites
items.text: Structure, tone, and imagery shaped for the sector: restaurant, hotel, studio, gym, or brand.

items.title: Conversion paths
items.text: A clear hierarchy, one main action, and short forms, so booking or writing is not an obstacle.

items.title: Fast development
items.text: Light interfaces, optimised images, and comfortable reading on a phone, where many decisions happen.

items.title: Multilingual websites
items.text: I design and build sites in multiple languages, with carefully crafted translations and international SEO (hreflang).

items.q: How long does a project take?
items.a: It depends on the scope. A site with a few sections takes a number of weeks, from the first conversation to launch.

items.q: Do you start from a template?
items.a: No. Each project starts with listening, structure, and an interface designed for that audience.

items.q: Which languages do you work in?
items.a: I communicate with clients in Italian, English, and Spanish. I can still design and build multilingual websites, with carefully crafted translations and international SEO.
Use the contact form. I reply with a reading of the scope, not a blind quote.

newsletter.title: A note, when there is something worth saying.
newsletter.text: No automated sequences. If you leave your email, I write when I publish a useful note.
